title: rulecad optimisation problem
description: A part to optimise, flat (2D) or solid (3D), in projects/<project>/problems/<name>.json: where material may go, what must stay solid or empty, where it's held and loaded, and what it's made of. Numbers are expressions, as in objects: of its variables and the rule sets it uses. cad optimise runs it; a design reads the result through a variable of type problem.

uses.description: Rule sets: the material's, the printer's, the part's own

variants.description: Named settings of variables with tweak ranges, picked as name:variant

material.description: A rule set with modulus (MPa), poisson and, for safety factors, strength (MPa)

cell.description: The grid's cell size, mm: smaller is finer and slower

volume.description: The share of the space to fill, 0 to 1 (keep regions count towards it): the stiffest layout that fills it. Give this or a stress limit

stress.description: A limit on von Mises stress (MPa), such as "pla.strength / 3": the lightest layout that keeps every cell under it (Senhora et al. 2020). Give this or a volume. A mechanism (with output) fills its volume as before and is checked against the limit at its input force: its peak, and the input force and output travel that reach the limit

strain.description: A strain limit in place of stress, a share of the length (0.02 is 2%), such as "pla.strength / pla.modulus / 2": the stress limit is it times the material's modulus. Most use for a mechanism, whose hinges bend

filter.description: Filter radius, mm: about the thinnest member (default a cell and a half, and never under two of the printer's lines)

projection.description: Sharpen the result to solid and empty (default true)

keep.description: Must stay solid: bosses round bolt holes

avoid.description: Must stay empty: holes, clearances (avoid wins over keep)

cases.description: Each load case's weight in the optimisation (default 1); 0 analyses it without optimising for it

smooth.description: Smoothing passes for the outline (2D) or surface (3D), default 4

min_area.description: Holes and islands smaller than this (mm²) are dropped

fine.description: 3D: the surface drawn on cells this many times finer than the problem's (default 1.25)

tip.description: 3D with an overhang direction: faces the smoothing left steeper than the printer's limit are tipped back to it as well (off by default: tipped corners can leave dips that slice as islands, and the sliced overhang is no smaller for it; the bracket example's 160 mm² of lean is the same either way)

reduce.description: 3D: fewer triangles, the surface kept within this many mm of where it was drawn, closed, and no more overhang or tips than it had. 0.1 mm (a quarter of a print line) unless given; false keeps every triangle the surface was drawn with

critical.description: Safety-critical (a pedal, a lever, a bracket that holds people): parts analysed under it are reported unverified until a test or an independent analysis is recorded against them

overhang.description: 3D: printable this way up ('+z', '-y', …), or a variable holding it, or 'none': only material supported from below at 45° or less

symmetry.description: The same either side of the grid's middle planes, and each half or quarter turn about its middle. The grid is centred on the space and keep regions (in 3D, except along an overhang's build direction). Keep and avoid regions stay as given. A mirror or turn that would swap the side a part is milled from, the way a mould is drawn off or the build direction for its opposite (or a quarter turn that moves it onto another axis) is refused by name; a mould in two halves parted at the grid's middle can be mirrored or half turned across its draw.

mirror.description: The axes mirrored across: 'x', 'xy', 'xyz' (2D: x and y)

turns.description: The same each half turn (2) or quarter turn (4) about the middle; a quarter turn needs the grid as wide both ways across its axis

axis.description: 3D: the axis turns are about (default z)

extrude.description: One section all along this axis: a part cut from a bar, an extrusion or a plate of the profile

mill.description: Milled from this side ('+z': the tool cuts down from above): no undercuts, so a cell is as solid as every cell between it and the tool. Not with overhang or cast. Rules: mill-3axis

cast.description: Cast or moulded: in a mould drawn off one way ('+z'), or in two halves drawn off both ways along an axis from a parting plane. No undercuts from the draw; draft is left to the drawing. Not with overhang or mill. Rules: mould-injection

draw.description: The axis the halves are drawn off along

parting.description: The parting plane, mm along draw (default the space's middle)

voids.description: Enclosed voids in the result: allowed (the default), or refused, for metal powder bed printing (powder left inside can't be got out) or a casting's trapped core: cad optimise then reports each as an error with its volume and where it is. Rules: dmls

output.description: A mechanism's output: where it should move, along one axis, against a spring. The first load is then the input.

anchor.description: In place of at: another design's anchor, object.anchor, where it is as that design is built (x and y of it in a flat problem). A cylinder lies along the anchor's axis unless it names one. Move the anchor and the problem moves with it. A design built from this problem can't be named: name what it's fixed to

direction.description: Which way it should move: along one axis, like [-1, 0]

spring.description: The spring it works against, N/mm

input_spring.description: With output: a spring the input pushes against, N/mm

at.description: The centre, mm: [x, y] in 2D, [x, y, z] in 3D

anchor.description: In place of at: another design's anchor, object.anchor, where it is as that design is built (x and y of it in a flat problem). A cylinder lies along the anchor's axis unless it names one. Move the anchor and the problem moves with it. A design built from this problem can't be named: name what it's fixed to

r.description: A circle's or ball's radius, or a cylinder's

part.description: A named part of another design in the project, as it's built: object.part. In a flat (2D) problem, its section halfway up (a plate's outline, its holes open)

teardrop.description: 3D: a 45° point on the cylinder that way, so it prints without support: down for a boss (its underside), up for a hole (its roof). up and down follow the problem's overhang (+z when it's free); along the cylinder's axis it has none
